conditions: Ideal thin lens in the paraxial approximation, same medium on both sides; real object/image distances positive, virtual distances negative; converging f positive, diverging f negative; finite nonzero f, d_o and d_i.
spoken_aliases: one divided by f equals one divided by d sub letter o plus one divided by d sub letter i
the reciprocal of the focal length equals the reciprocal of the object distance plus the reciprocal of the image distance

evidence: In paraxial optics use the signed ray-height/slope transformation of a thin lens: the outgoing slope equals the incoming slope minus ray height divided by f. A ray from the on-axis object at lens height y has incoming slope y/d_o and outgoing slope -y/d_i. Equating and dividing by nonzero y gives 1/f=1/d_o+1/d_i.
